construct: Hereditary spherocytosis results from defects in red-cell membrane/cytoskeletal proteins such as ankyrin, spectrin, band 3, or protein 4.2. Loss of vertical membrane-cytoskeleton integrity causes progressive membrane loss, reduced surface-area-to-volume ratio, spherocyte formation, decreased deformability, and splenic sequestration with extravascular hemolysis.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Familial Coombs-negative extravascular hemolysis with splenomegaly, spherocytes, reticulocytosis, indirect hyperbilirubinemia, and increased MCHC strongly indicates hereditary spherocytosis.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia also produces spherocytes, but it is usually direct-antiglobulin positive and lacks the inherited family pattern.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The family history plus negative DAT and classic membrane-loss laboratory phenotype make hereditary spherocytosis uniquely best.
